record.paper_title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces
record.context_brief: Implication between the separable and nonseparable basis problems
record.original_question: Does a positive answer to the separable model problem for Ep = Lp([0,1]^2), namely the existence of an unconditional basis (fn) union (gn) whose fn part spans the first-coordinate subspace Fp and has the same unconditional constant as the full basis, formally imply a positive answer to the nonseparable problem asking whether Lp({-1,1}^{omega_1}) has an unconditional basis for 1 <= p < infinity and p not equal to 2?

evidence.quote: We do not know of whether an affirmative solution to Problem 7 formally implies an affirmative solution to Problem 6.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix $1 \le p < \infty$ with $p \ne 2$. Let $E_p = L_p([0,1]^2)$ (with Lebesgue measure), and let $F_p \subset E_p$ denote the closed subspace of functions depending only on the first coordinate (so $F_p$ is isometric to $L_p[0,1]$).

Consider the following two questions:

(A) Separable model problem: Does $E_p$ admit an unconditional Schauder basis of the form $(f_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}} \cup (g_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ such that $(f_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ is an unconditional basis of $F_p$ whose unconditional constant equals that of the full basis $(f_n)\cup(g_n)$ of $E_p$?

(B) Nonseparable problem: Does $L_p(\{-1,1\}^{\omega_1})$ (with the product of uniform probability measures on $\{-1,1\}$, indexed by the first uncountable ordinal $\omega_1$) admit an unconditional basis (in the appropriate uncountable Schauder sense, i.e., a transfinite unconditional basis indexed by a set of cardinality $\aleph_1$)?

Question: Does an affirmative answer to (A) formally imply an affirmative answer to (B)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether $L_p(\{-1,1\}^{\omega_1})$ has an unconditional basis (for $1\le p<\infty$, $p\ne 2$) is a well-known long-standing open problem in the theory of nonseparable $L_p$-spaces, and the implication between the separable model version and the nonseparable version is explicitly noted as unknown. No published resolution of either the implication or the nonseparable problem itself was found.

status_evidence.title: On two long standing open problems on Lp-spaces (zbMATH 7252022)
status_evidence.snippet: Survey discussing open problems on unconditional bases in separable and nonseparable Lp-spaces.
status_evidence.claim: The implication between the separable model formulation and the nonseparable unconditional basis problem for Lp({-1,1}^{omega_1}) is stated as not known.

status_evidence.title: Unconditional basic sequences in function spaces with applications to Orlicz spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on unconditional basic sequences in function spaces; the existence of unconditional bases in nonseparable Lp spaces is not established.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to treat the existence of unconditional bases in nonseparable Lp spaces as unresolved.
